tracks.title: Python
tracks.course: Introduction to Python Programming for AI
tracks.blurb: Functions, lists, dictionaries, strings and comprehensions, built up to from-scratch exam questions.

tracks.title: Intelligent Systems
tracks.blurb: Search, game trees, propositional logic and rule-based reasoning, all traced by hand.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.summary: def, parameters vs arguments, return vs print, None, local scope
objectives: You can write a function with parameters, type hints and a return value.
You can tell return from print and predict when a call gives back None.
You can explain why a local variable is gone once the call ends.

lessons.title: Lists basics
lessons.summary: indexing, negative indexes, slicing, len, in, append, insert, pop, remove
objectives: You can read any element or slice of a list, including with negative indexes.
You can predict what len, in, append, insert, pop and remove do to a list.

lessons.title: Looping over lists
lessons.summary: for x in lst, range(len()), enumerate, and the accumulator patterns
objectives: You can choose between for x in lst, range(len(lst)) and enumerate.
You can write the accumulator patterns from scratch: sum, count, max and filter into a new list.

lessons.title: Mutability
lessons.summary: aliasing vs copying, changing a list vs returning a new one, nested lists
objectives: You can predict what happens when two names point at the same list.
You can write a function that changes a list in place and one that returns a new list, and say which is which.
You can read and update a nested list.

lessons.group: Week 4: dictionaries, tuples, sets and strings
lessons.title: Dictionaries basics
lessons.summary: keys and values, get, in, items(), adding and updating
objectives: You can create, read, add and update key-value pairs.
You can avoid a KeyError with in or get.
You can loop over a dictionary with items().

lessons.group: Week 4: dictionaries, tuples, sets and strings
lessons.title: Dictionary patterns
lessons.summary: counting, grouping into a dict of lists, inverting, dicts with functions
objectives: You can count things with a dictionary.
You can group items into a dictionary of lists.
You can invert a dictionary and write functions that take or return one.

lessons.group: Week 4: dictionaries, tuples, sets and strings
lessons.title: Tuples and sets
lessons.summary: immutability, unpacking, set operations, when to use which
objectives: You can unpack a tuple and explain why it cannot be changed.
You can use set operations to answer membership and overlap questions.
You can choose between a list, tuple, set and dictionary for a task.

lessons.group: Week 4: dictionaries, tuples, sets and strings
lessons.title: Strings
lessons.summary: slicing again, split, join, strip, replace, lower, looping over characters, f-strings
objectives: You can slice and loop over a string the way you do with a list.
You can use split, join, strip, replace and lower in a small text task.
You can build output with f-strings.

lessons.group: Week 4: dictionaries, tuples, sets and strings
lessons.title: Comprehensions
lessons.summary: list and dict comprehensions, with if
objectives: You can rewrite a loop that builds a list as a list comprehension.
You can add an if filter to a comprehension.
You can build a dictionary with a dict comprehension.

lessons.title: Conditionals and loops, reviewed
lessons.summary: while vs for, break, nested loops
objectives: You can choose between while and for and say why.
You can trace break and nested loops by hand.

lessons.title: From-scratch drill
lessons.summary: functions, lists and dictionaries mixed, in exam style
objectives: You can write a full function from a blank cell without notes.
You can combine lists, dictionaries and functions in one solution.

lessons.title: Mini mock
lessons.summary: a 45-minute practical-style set, then a review of your mistakes
objectives: You can finish a practical-style set within 45 minutes.
You can find your own weak spots from your mistakes list.

lessons.group: Week 1: state spaces and uninformed search
lessons.title: Uninformed search
lessons.summary: state spaces, BFS, DFS, iterative deepening and uniform cost, with a properties table
objectives: You can describe a problem as a state space with states, actions and a goal test.
You can trace BFS, DFS, iterative deepening and uniform cost search by hand.
You can compare them on completeness, optimality, time and space.

lessons.title: Informed search
lessons.summary: heuristics, admissible vs consistent, greedy best-first vs A*, traced by hand
objectives: You can check whether a heuristic is admissible and whether it is consistent.
You can trace greedy best-first search and A* with f = g + h by hand.
You can say when A* is guaranteed to find the cheapest path.

lessons.title: Adversarial search
lessons.summary: minimax and alpha-beta pruning by hand on game trees
objectives: You can compute minimax values on a game tree by hand.
You can run alpha-beta pruning and mark exactly which branches are cut.

lessons.title: Logic 1: meaning
lessons.summary: syntax vs semantics, interpretations, models, satisfiable and valid, entailment, truth tables
objectives: You can tell syntax, semantics and calculus apart.
You can decide with a truth table whether a formula is satisfiable, valid or unsatisfiable.
You can check entailment by comparing models.

lessons.title: Logic 2: CNF
lessons.summary: converting a formula to conjunctive normal form, step by step
objectives: You can convert a propositional formula to CNF one step at a time.
You can spot which step went wrong in a faulty conversion.

lessons.title: Logic 3: DPLL
lessons.summary: DPLL by hand, and the pseudocode from memory
objectives: You can run DPLL by hand with unit propagation, pure literals and splitting.
You can fill in the DPLL pseudocode from memory.

lessons.title: Rules and knowledge graphs
lessons.summary: modus ponens, and-elimination, De Morgan, forward reasoning, RDF triples
objectives: You can apply modus ponens, and-elimination and De Morgan in a forward-reasoning chain.
You can read and write facts as RDF triples.
You can derive new facts from a small knowledge graph.

lessons.title: Mixed exam drill
lessons.summary: a mini mock across every topic, plus exam strategy
objectives: You can switch between search, logic and reasoning questions in one sitting.
You can plan your time across the whole exam.

lessons.title: Exam warm-up
lessons.summary: ten quick questions across every topic
objectives: You can recall the key definitions and properties without notes.
You can walk in knowing which traps to watch for.
